To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CD4+ cells isolated directly from the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of elite suppressors (ES), viremic patients (VP), and uninfected controls (UC) are all susceptible to HIV-1 productive infection.
CD4+T cells from HIV-1 elite suppressors are fully susceptible to HIV-1 infection in vitro.
the CD4+ T cell population from ES is fully susceptible to HIV-1 infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms that control HIV replication and the identification of new therapeutic targets to treat HIV infection.
the mechanisms of HIV-1 infection and pathogenesis, and with the design of novel therapeutic approaches to HIV-1 infection.
the mechanisms that underlie elite control of HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD4 T cells of ES patients are not resistant to HIV-1 infection and replication.
the CD4+ T cell from the ES is as susceptible to HIV-1 infection as any CD4+ T-cell from a viremic patient.

the CD4+ T cell compartment in ES is as susceptible as that of viremic individuals and uninfected controls to HIV-1 infection, and that the mechanisms of elite suppression of HIV-1 replication must therefore be sought in the other compartments of the immune system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD4+T cells from ES are not resistant to infection, and that ES may be able to control infection through mechanisms that are not related to the intrinsic resistance of CD4+T cell to infection.
ES cells are fully susceptible to HIV-1 infection, and the mechanism of control must therefore lie downstream of viral entry.
